reason: Unsafe behaviour left uncorrected: 'It was a smelly dog, but it was friendly. Henry patted its soft fur.'
Confusing name switch and reasoning chain: 'Linlin wanted to buy the basket' and 'The last number was six both times. So the green basket really had more.'
Stranger dog jumps at child, then petting it is shown as fine: 'But the dog licked his hand. It was a friendly dog. Aiden laughed and patted its soft ears.'
Confusing ending: 'Under the mirror were five letters... "R. O. O. K." ... "N is for Nyah!"' does not spell her name and loses the child.
Confusing color claim for a color-words story: red plus blue paint 'The frog turned green!'
Confusing plot: librarian says 'You can take it home' but then 'Theodore gave back the book at the desk,' after he 'hid it under his coat.'
Abstract idea of copied emotions stated as a metaphor: 'Faces were like a magnet... One face pulled another face to it.'
Too long and episodic for age 3: 12 paragraphs stacking balloon, loud dog, and 'She grabbed the blue chalk without asking' episodes.
Unsafe act shown as fine: 'Mom unbuckled her belt and leaned back' to get the toy on the way there.
Hard word and a nonsensical abstract line: 'auditorium' and 'It was like a puzzle. And the answer was true.'
3-year-old handles a flame, shown as fine: "Lillian touched her candle to the big girl's candle" and waves her hand behind it.
Confusing eye test: 'The light looked the same... Then the light looked different. Covering made it change!... Now he saw two lights.'
Long, wandering plot: senses exam, then an unrelated tower-physics detour ('She spun the top block. It wobbled... Then it tipped.'), then bread.
Muddled plot: the dog splashes the swing yet 'The swing dried in the sun', then a non-sequitur 'Eleanor gave the child her hat.'
Abstract comparisons for a 3-year-old: 'too long and too thick, like a big sandwich he could not bite' and 'It was like pushing a swing and the swing went.'
Unsupervised learner swimming shown as fine: 'Dad waved from his beach chair' while she kicks away from the wall and races to the steps.
Two stories glued together; it restarts mid-text ('in the soft white yard.Brielle woke up.'), doubling length and confusing the plot.
Confusing timeline in a time-words story: he took the book home, yet 'You gave it back yesterday. Now it is here today.'
Confusing non sequiturs: 'I found a tiny marble in one.' and 'My sock was squishy last night,' plus a baby never introduced.
Confusing forced word and jumbled weather: 'It made a big triangle of colors over the houses,' then snow right after sun and rain.
Confusing plot: Grandpa calls 'Grandma, come look!' then 'But Grandpa had a trick of his own' and the Grandma thread vanishes.
Long and wandering for age 3: senses game drifts into 'He wanted to swing his arms like a big wind', a milk spill, a lesson 'Mistakes happen when we learn.' and a cat.
Muddled opposites logic a child cannot follow: 'It went wide across her teddy's cup' and 'Big cup, slow tea. Small cup, fast tea!'
Tangled plot and forced wording: Tom 'has green' yet they must mix it, then he has none; 'It hopped on the paper, in her mind' and 'It was not mean to take the paint. It was nice.'
Unsafe fire play shown as fun: 'a paper flower fell... landed right on her lamp. The flame made the paper glow warm and pink... Nova laughed and clapped her hands.'
Past-perfect flashback is hard for a 3-year-old to follow: 'He had grabbed, and Ben had cried. Then Ben gave him the truck. Alexis had given it back.'
Unresolved plot: the dog book is never found and it ends on a stranger's puppy, 'Can we take him home for a visit?'
Confusing plot logic: 'Let's ask the singing corner' and 'Singing made us hungry for books,' then the too-high book is suddenly on a low shelf.
Confusing pretend-play logic: 'Well, Mia made him cry.' and 'Then she stopped crying the bear.'
Death theme left unexplained for a 3-4-year-old: 'Ivy went to the cemetery... near Grandpa Ben's stone.'
Muddled turn order and grab never addressed: 'When Noah waited, he got his turn again.' then 'Your turn now,' to Ben.
Meandering plot (teddy truck, Dad retrieving a toy from the road) and wry aside 'It waved too, or maybe that was just the wind.'
Disjointed scenes and confusing lines like 'Her friend Sam held a small block. Hers was big.' and 'the fast hum told her when it was done.'
Muddled ending: Luke gets to take the book home, then 'handed the book to the librarian. I'll bring it back soon', leaving who has the book unclear.
Confusing, hard-to-follow logic: 'The bus door waved back, kind of' and 'That's the magic of school'; plot jumps from bus to gate to horse picture.
Confusing lemon-juice step: 'Then the paper turned pink where the lemon had dried,' plus forced 'I build a rainbow too.'
Confusing tangent and forced word in one long block: 'She even left one for the tooth fairy cup where her loose tooth had been,' 'Grandma did say.'
Story text is garbled and restarts mid-sentence: 'TeddBlake wanted to be a mommy today,' so the plot repeats and tangles.
Unclear, possibly unsafe tree scene: 'The wind blew again. Amira held on tight with her mittens... she did not let go.'
Tangled calendar logic ('in two days' said yesterday, then 'one empty square left... That square is today!') plus abstract aside 'One thing made another thing happen, just like that.'
Confusing time sequence: 'watered her seed again after dinner time, when the class had a snack. Then she went home to eat dinner.'
Confusing counting: five apples go in the bag, then 'At home, he would eat one apple. Nine would be left.'; a lamp tangent in the store adds clutter.
Plot drifts to a bus button and a stranger's fish and chips, and 'Will it hurt?' about the dentist is never really answered.
Confusing narration: 'The green apples were hiding under his hat brim. No, wait. They were just sitting in a pile.'
Nonsense forced line 'The ball did not bite the dog's nose. It was soft!', and Owen coaxes a lone unknown dog with no one correcting it.
Mixed safety message in a hot-things story: 'The man touched the grill, and the hot dogs got warm,' then the child takes food from that stranger.
Plot makes no sense to a child: 'She stepped on the sticky spot too. Her shoe stuck, just like his.' She steps in the glue on purpose, and no reason is given.
Long, and the second girl's subplot is confusing: 'The girl was holding a book about fire trucks. It was not the same one. It was a different one, and she looked sad.'
Unsafe behaviour shown as fine: a 3-year-old cups her hands around a lit candle flame ('So Lennon put her hands around it too').
The coin-machine part is confusing and makes no sense: 'It made a round shape, like a triangle but round. Then it gave back paper money.'
A time-words story that misuses its target word, 'Tomorrow morning, Milo came back to school.', and adds an adult idiom, 'Pay attention to that bean'.
Nonsensical fix a child cannot follow: 'The air made the curtain spin and puff out wide. When the curtain puffed, the TV showed through the gap!'
Tangled plot: Layla grabs the truck, then says 'You can have a long turn... I need to wrap a present at the art table first,' and Ben's line 'The truck goes far when I share it' makes no sense.
Confusing setting: Asher gets the book at 'the store' but 'It had to come back on the stamp day,' a borrowing idea that does not fit a store.
Many long appositive sentences and figurative lines, e.g. 'She wanted to find the letter B, the one that started her own name.' and 'The sounds fit together like puzzle pieces.'
Name-writing story spells Lucas wrong ('L, then U, then C, then A... Four letters'), which would confuse a child learning their name; several long sentences too.
Unsafe act not corrected as a safety matter: 'He put the seed in his ear. No, that was wrong. Ears hear sounds, not seeds.'
Muddled plot: 'Grandma hung it over a chair... Grandma put the sweater on the chair... That is my chair!' is hard to follow.
